definitions.explanation: A swordsman of the early Edo period, famous for fighting with two swords and for never losing a duel. He wrote The Book of Five Rings ({五輪書|ごりんのしょ}), a treatise on strategy still read today.

examples.japanese: {宮本武蔵|みやもとむさし}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{有名|ゆうめい}→有名：01106_yuumei⟧な{剣豪|けんごう}だ。
examples.english: Miyamoto Musashi is a famous master swordsman.

examples.japanese: {宮本武蔵|みやもとむさし}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{二刀流|にとうりゅう}→二刀流：15543_nitouryuu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{戦|たたか}った→戦う：02071_tatakau⟧。
examples.english: Miyamoto Musashi fought with two swords.

examples.japanese: {巌流島|がんりゅうじま}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{宮本武蔵|みやもとむさし}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{佐々木小次郎|ささきこじろう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{決闘|けっとう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{小説|しょうせつ}→小説：01434_shousetsu⟧や⟦{映画|えいが}→映画：02273_eiga⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{何度|なんど}→何度：17592_nando⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{描|えが}かれて→描く：02013_egaku⟧きた。
examples.english: The duel between Miyamoto Musashi and Sasaki Kojirō on Ganryūjima has been portrayed again and again in novels and films.

notes:
COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- ⟦{二刀流|にとうりゅう}→二刀流：15543_nitouryuu⟧: two-sword style; now also an athlete who does two things at once, such as a pitcher who also bats
- {五輪書|ごりんのしょ}: The Book of Five Rings, his writings on strategy
- {巌流島|がんりゅうじま}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{決闘|けっとう}: his 1612 duel with {佐々木小次郎|ささきこじろう}

CULTURAL NOTE:
His popular image comes largely from {吉川英治|よしかわえいじ}'s novel {宮本武蔵|みやもとむさし} (1935–1939), which later inspired the manga バガボンド.
